conviction_note: The half's operating lines (occupancy, rent roll, lettings) were pre-released on 15 Oct and the stock fell 5.8% that day. Since then it has lagged London office peers by about 12-15 points, so most of the visible bad news looks priced. What is still new is the 30 Sep valuation and NTA, the interim dividend (the 1.2x cover policy implies a cut from 9.4p), any number put on the FY27 'substantial step down', and refinancing. The evidence leans slightly negative: disposals went 28% below book and Q2 lettings value fell a third year on year. Against that sit a falling-but-sizeable short (6.76%), Saba at 29.7% pushing for disposals and buybacks, and peers' valuations up. Hence p_up 46 on an abs move of 5.0, giving -0.4. The findings sum to -0.9 because they are sized one at a time and not netted against the priced underperformance; the scaled number is the smaller of the two for exactly that reason.

positioning_check: FCA aggregated net short 6.76% at 2026-11-11, down from 6.89% (-0.13pp, slight covering), per the baseline from https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv. findings.finding: The company has signalled that its 30 Sep 2026 valuation will come under pressure. Q1 disposals were agreed 'at an aggregate discount to March 2026 book value of 28.0%', and some buyers' pricing has been 'substantially below book value'. That points to another write-down and lower EPRA NTA in the release, after the -4.0% / NTA -6.8% half a year earlier.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HY 2025 (19 Nov 2025): valuation -4.0% underlying, NTA -6.8%, stock -5.34% over the window. FY26 (10 Jun 2026): valuation -7.0% for the year; the reaction is not in the baseline because the window used 2025-06-05 for FY25.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell 5.8% on 15 Oct and has lagged Landsec, British Land, Derwent and GPE by about 12-15 points since. The size of the write-down and NTA is still unknown. At about 345p against a last-reported NTA well above 600p, the market already holds a large discount, which caps what a valuation miss can do.
findings.independence: The disposals were small (£12.6m), so they are a weak read on a £2.1bn book. The FY26 statement shows ERV per sq ft -3.8% over the year: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/workspace-group--wkp/transforming-to-an-earnings-focused-business/9610047

findings.finding: Peer valuations at the same 30 Sep date are firm. Landsec's HY (13 Nov 2026) shows a £88m valuation surplus and London office ERV +2.9% over six months; British Land's H1 pre-close shows values +1.5% and ERV +3.0%. Workspace's own new all-inclusive lettings are 8% (completed) and 14% (under offer) above ERV. Together these argue the yield side of Workspace's valuation is stable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not observed separately. In HY 2025 the equivalent yield came in 17bps while ERV fell 2.3%; ERV was the driver.
findings.why_not_priced: Peers have re-rated on this (LAND 651->695p, BLND 422->434p since mid-Oct) while WKP fell, so the market is treating Workspace's secondary small-unit segment as decoupled from prime. If the valuers give WKP even a stable yield, the write-down could come in smaller than the 15-Oct sell-off implied. This is a proxy with weak transmission, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: British Land H1 pre-close (values +1.5%, ERV +3.0%): https://fashionunited.uk/news/business/british-land-forecasts-166-million-pounds-underlying-profit-for-h1-fy27/2026101690878 ; WKP's own above-ERV lettings in the Q2 RNS

findings.finding: The interim dividend is set to be cut from last year's 9.4p. The board's policy is 'earnings cover of 1.2x for FY26 onwards', and FY27 trading profit is guided to a 'substantial step down' (emerging consensus c.£47m against £60.5m).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY26 dividend fell 8.1% to 26.1p, announced with the April profit warning, when the stock fell about 15%. The HY 2025 interim was held at 9.4p.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the policy is public and the cut follows mechanically. Only the size of the interim is unknown. Sized near zero because it lands inside what the company has guided.
findings.independence: The consensus figure comes from a search snippet of the Berenberg note on hl.co.uk, which returned 404: https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/share-tips/stockbroker-tips/berenberg-lowers-target-price-on-workspace-ahead-of-period-of-transition

findings.finding: Q2 leasing momentum fell sharply, which puts FY27 earnings at risk from the forward rent roll. New lettings rental value was £4.9m in Q2 against £7.8m in Q1 and £7.3m a year earlier; viewings were 322 against 519; August was 'subdued'. The release could quantify the FY27 step down at or below consensus, or trim it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The April 2026 Q4 update warning of a 'substantial step down' took the stock down about 15%; the 15 Oct Q2 update took it down 5.8%. Guidance and activity lines have moved this stock far more than results days (+1.1, -1.6, -5.3).
findings.why_not_priced: The activity data is public and the stock fell on it. What has not been tested is whether management converts weaker lettings into a lower or quantified FY27 number. With no number yet given and consensus at about £47m, a quantified guide below that would be new. The September pick-up (79 lettings, £2.3m) and above-ERV pricing could equally let them hold the line, so the sign is uncertain and the size is held below 1.
findings.independence: The April profit warning coverage gives JPM's implied 18-26% cut to forecasts: https://uk.marketscreener.com/news/uk-office-space-firm-workspace-warns-of-substantial-profit-drop-for-fiscal-2027-ce7e50d2dd8cf127

findings.finding: Positioning leans against further downside. Saba Capital holds 29.73% combined (18.66% shares plus 11.07% instruments at 28-Oct-2026) and is pushing for disposals and buybacks after losing the July AGM board vote. The disclosed short is 6.76% and slightly covering. WKP has lagged its London peers by about 12-15 points since the 14 Oct close.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None observed on a results day.
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline lean (+3.17, mostly the short-squeeze component) already carries the short. What it does not carry is Saba's near-30% economic stake and the relative de-rating. If the release brings any capital return or disposal progress near book, a 6.8% short in a $1m/day name has little liquidity to cover into.
findings.independence: AGM result showing Saba's resolutions defeated (13.3% support excluding Saba): https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/workspace-group--wkp/results-of-annual-general-meeting/9685044 ; FCA register via the baseline

findings.finding: Management flagged a refinancing still to come against higher rates: 'Against a backdrop of challenging market conditions and the recent material increase in bond yields, we remain focused on our upcoming refinancings and our credit rating.' The release may set out a refinancing at a higher cost of debt.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None observed. In Nov 2025 a £215m bank facility extension came alongside the HY results with no visible separate effect.
findings.why_not_priced: This refinances existing maturities and is not distress: the company says maturities are covered to March 2028 from undrawn facilities. The open question is the coupon, which would hit FY28 interest. It is sized small because whether anything is announced in the window is uncertain.
findings.independence: FY26 outlook: 'we can cover all of our debt maturities until March 2028 using existing undrawn facilities, we are actively reviewing our refinancing options' https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/workspace-group--wkp/transforming-to-an-earnings-focused-business/9610047

outside_window.finding: Saba's next step (a further requisition or a move past 30%) could force a Rule 9 offer or a capital return. Nothing is dated in the window.

baseline_tension: The lean is +3.17 (short squeeze) and the 20-day run-up is +1.8% (5-day -3.9%). My findings lean slightly negative, against the lean, but the 15-Oct sell-off and relative underperformance suggest most of the negatives are priced. The scaled number is therefore close to zero (-0.4) rather than the -0.9 findings sum.
